newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alfa subsidiaries consider debt issues.
newsitem.headline: Alfa subsidiaries consider debt issues.

text.p: Industrial conglomerate ALFA subsidiaries, Hylsamex and Alpek, could place about $350 million in debt in 1997, a company executive said on Thursday.
The steel producing subsidiary, Hylsamex, is studying refinancing $100 million, while petrochemical unit Alpek is looking at refinancing $250 million, finance director Alfonso Gonzalez Migoya said.
"It is very likely Hylsamex will have to complete its refinancing program... which is will leave it with another $100 million for this year," he told reporters in a telephone conference.
He said the main part of Hylsamex's refinancing plan is aimed at its February 1998 payment of an outstanding $175 million Eurobond.
He added Hylsamex could refinance an additional $100 million from diverse operations such as syndicated credits or credits backed by exports, he said.
He said that while Alpek plans to refinance $250 million in debt during the year, it may not necessarily go to credit markets in 1997.
Alpek has a good financial picture and a strong cash flow that will permit it to wait until 1998 if conditions in 1997 are not attractive, the executive said.
